nl.text:
Let `A` be the filtered anchored powerset on the left.  Reindex each `P ∈ A` by `X := P.erase a` and `j := X.card`.  Since `a ∈ P`, `P = insert a X`; from `P ⊆ C` obtain `X ⊆ C.erase a`, and `P.card ≤ d + 1` becomes `j < d + 1`, hence `j ∈ Finset.range (d + 1)`.  Conversely, for `j` in that range and `X ∈ (C.erase a).powersetCard j`, `insert a X` belongs to `A` using `ha`.  These constructions are inverse, so `Finset.sum_bij` gives a reindexing of the left sum by `j` and the exact-cardinality subfinsets of `C.erase a`.

For each such fiber, `Finset.card_erase_of_mem` and the range bound normalize its weight to `Nat.choose U.card (d - j)`.  The fiber has cardinality `Nat.choose (C.erase a).card j` by `Finset.card_powersetCard`.  Apply `Finset.sum_congr` to replace every fiber sum by this cardinality times its constant weight, yielding exactly the displayed `Finset.range (d + 1)` convolution.  Filter/powerset membership simplifications and the bijection witnesses are local finite-set steps; no extra hypothesis is used.

# lean-constellation target: `anchoredPowerset_chooseSum_reindex`

For a type with decidable equality, finite sets `C` and `U`, an anchor `a ∈ C`, and a natural number
d,
`∑ P ∈ C.powerset.filter (fun P => a ∈ P ∧ P.card ≤ d + 1), Nat.choose U.card (d + 1 - P.card) = ∑ j
∈ Finset.range (d + 1), Nat.choose (C.erase a).card j * Nat.choose U.card (d - j)`.
The reindexing sends an anchored subset P to `P.erase a`; grouping by `j = (P.erase a).card`
preserves the displayed natural-number subtraction indices and needs no hypothesis beyond `a ∈ C`.
